text:
House Thream’s rule from year 2 to 51 was defined by a succession of strongmen and a persistent war with the Goummeidale Compact. The period began with an alliance to the Kraeford Compact, but the house quickly lost its grip on Sti Seam. The conflict with Goummeidale lasted four years, ending in a peace that left House Thream defeated and stripped of territory. The house survived through a series of violent successions, where rulers were frequently murdered or cast out, and through the return of exiles who restored its strength. By the end, the house had lost Sti Seam permanently, suffered a famine, and seen its internal stability erode into a cycle of failed attempts on its captain’s life.

Freamteas Kraeth died in Loufell in year 3, and Kokaes Threll married Keath Daendro to bind the house to the Kraeford Compact. The Goummeidale Compact declared war on House Thream for Sti Seam in year 3, defeating them at that site with 35 dead. Bran Nas took the seat by the strongest claim in year 3. House Thream raided Goummeidale in year 4, carrying off 49 grain and killing 54, and defeated the Goummeidale Compact at Sti Seam in year 4 with 29 dead. They defeated them again at Sti Seam in year 5 with 24 dead. Bran Nas died in Loufell in year 6, and the Goummeidale Compact defeated House Thream at Sti Seam with 20 dead, taking the site from them. Kokaes Threll contested the claim of Ma Graltaeld in year 6, took the seat, and cast Ma Graltaeld out.

Vinbeil Real returned from exile in year 7 and took the seat in year 8 after Fous Bo murdered Kokaes Threll. House Thream made peace with the Goummeidale Compact after four years of war in year 7. Fous Bo’s conspiracy was uncovered in year 10, and he was cast out. Vinbeil Real died in Loufell in year 17, and Laenroull Re took the seat. Kraedren Waeld and Freindmald Beindlea returned from exile in year 20 and year 25 respectively. Reafaeth Geall murdered Laenroull Re in Loufell in year 26 and took the seat. He married Vasgou Raend in year 27, binding the house to the Goummeidale Compact. Reafaeth Geall was cast out in year 29 after an attempt on Skullhein Threill failed.

Waeld Dould took the seat in year 29. A famine at Loufell in year 31 killed 31 people. Vasgou Raend was killed by Rateal Fototh in Loufell in year 31. Frouldtoun Dror returned from exile in year 31. House Thream raided Kreagemoor in year 33, carrying off 26 grain and killing 11, and swore an alliance with the Kreagemoor Covenant in year 35. Waeld Dould was cast out in year 49 after an attempt on Rateal Fototh failed. Gu Veam took the seat in year 49. Gu Veam was cast out in year 50 after another attempt on Rateal Fototh failed. Neti Gulmol took the seat in year 50. House Thream’s raid on Sti Seam was beaten off in year 51.

The Kraeford Compact’s decade from 42 to 51 was defined by external pressure and internal instability. At the start, the Compact was engaged in a war with the Goummeidale Compact that ended in exhaustion and peace in 42. The period saw two failed raids launched by the Kraeford Compact against Goummeidale targets, both beaten off. The seat passed between three rulers: Tas Pald, who was killed in 47; Saebull Kei, who took the seat that same year but was cast out in 50; and Grigun Thrundeith, who assumed the seat in 50 and held it until the period ended.

Tas Pald ruled until 47, when he was killed by Rateal Fototh at Kraeford. Saebull Kei took the seat immediately after Tas Pald’s death. In 48, the Goummeidale Compact raided Kraeford, killing 21 people but taking nothing. In 50, Saebull Kei attempted to kill Rateal Fototh; the attempt failed and was traced back to him. Saebull Kei was cast out for attempted murder, and Grigun Thrundeith took the seat. Waeld Dould returned from exile in 51 and took service with the Kraeford Compact.

In 51, the Goummeidale Compact declared war on the Kraeford Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Goummeidale Compact defeated the Kraeford Compact at Kraeford, with 136 dead. The Kraeford Compact had fought one battle and lost it. The period ended in 51 with Grigun Thrundeith still holding the seat.

The period from 42 to 51 was defined by internal instability and a sudden return to external aggression. The Goummeidale Compact began with a ruler already dead, leaving the seat to pass through three hands in ten years. Skullhein Threill was killed by Rateal Fototh in 42, and Haern Taethnum took the seat by right of birth. Haern’s rule ended when Rateal Fototh challenged him openly and won in 46, taking the seat by coup. Rateal held the seat until 51, when Theirnpae Gro challenged him openly, won, and took the seat. Theirnpae remained in power at the end of the period.

The Compact’s internal cohesion was fragile. Rateal Fototh had Tas Pald murdered at Kraeford in 47, and two of its own people were murdered from within. Two people were cast out: Gu Veam for losing an open challenge in 46, and Haern Taethnum for losing a coup in 46. The seat passed from one person to another three times inside this period. The Compact suffered four raids, all beaten off: by the Kraeford Compact at Sti Seam in 42 and Seithfaehollow in 45, and by House Thream at Kreagemoor in 42 and Sti Seam in 51. It sent out one raid, on Kraeford in 48, which got through but took nothing.

Disease and diplomacy marked the era’s other dimensions. Plague broke out at Seithfaehollow in 42, taking 83 lives, and returned in 43, killing 122 and causing 139 to flee. The Compact made peace with the Kraeford Compact after two years of war in 42. Marriages tied the Compact to other powers: Tas Pald married Theldsild Tripould in 43, binding the Compact to the Kraeford Compact; Saebull Kei married Thra Meil in 48, binding the Compact to the Kraeford Compact again; and Neti Gulmol married Meind Veild in 48, binding the Compact to House Thream. In 51, the Compact declared war on the Kraeford Compact over a long-standing grievance and defeated it at Kraeford, with 136 dead.

The Kraeford Compact’s twenty-year span from 22 to 41 was defined by a shift from aggressive expansion to catastrophic defeat. At the start, the Compact launched raids against its neighbors, carrying off grain from Kreagemoor and Ra Cut. By the end, it had lost a major settlement to the Goummeidale Compact and suffered two decisive military defeats. The period saw five rulers hold the seat, with power passing four times through death, exile, and succession. The Compact’s standing deteriorated from a position of offensive capability to one of territorial loss and heavy casualties.

Wun Thu ruled until his death in 31, after which Haern Taethnum took the seat. Taethnum’s rule was short and ended in 37 when he was cast out for attempting to kill Skullhein Threill. Duthturn Tend succeeded him, ruling until he was killed by Skullhein Threill in 39. Soth Soulol then took the seat, only to be killed by Skullhein Threill in 41. Tas Pald assumed the seat in 41 and held it at the period’s end. Two rulers were killed, one was cast out, one died, and one remained in power.

The Compact’s military fortunes reversed sharply. It sent five raids, three of which carried off plunder and two of which were beaten off. However, it suffered two raids from the Goummeidale Compact, which took grain from Kraeford and Seithfaehollow. In 40, the Goummeidale Compact declared war over a long-standing grievance and defeated the Kraeford Compact at Seithfaehollow, killing 199 and taking the settlement. A plague at Seithfaehollow that year killed 118 people. In 41, the Goummeidale Compact defeated the Kraeford Compact again at Kraeford, killing 162. The Compact lost Seithfaehollow and faced two battles, both lost to the Goummeidale Compact.

The period from 2 to 21 was defined by a volatile alliance with the Kraeford Compact and a protracted, inconclusive war with House Thream. The Goummeidale Compact began the era holding the seat through primogeniture, with Sealoll Lael already in power. The relationship with Kraeford was cemented by three marriages in 2, 5, and 15, creating a persistent diplomatic link. However, the Compact’s military posture was aggressive and often unsuccessful. It initiated one war in 3 over Sti Seam, which lasted four years and ended in exhaustion. During this conflict, the Compact won two battles but lost two others, failing to secure a decisive advantage. The war drained resources and contributed to a decline in standing, evidenced by a rebellion at Sti Seam in 7.

Internal stability was fragile. A conspiracy by Vinbeil Real against Sealoll Lael was uncovered in 5, leading to Real’s exile. The seat passed to Kaell Frouspim in 14 upon Lael’s death. The Compact suffered thirteen raids during the period, five of which carried off plunder. It sent out five raids, all of which succeeded in taking grain and killing inhabitants of Kraeford, Seithfaehollow, and Kreagemoor. Despite these successes, the Compact lost control of Kreagemoor in 8, which broke away to form the Kreagemoor Covenant. The Covenant and the Kraeford Compact both raided Compact territories, with most attacks beaten off or yielding nothing.

The era ended with the Goummeidale Compact still holding the seat, but its position was weakened. It had lost a territory to a new power and endured significant internal dissent, with four individuals courted away from the ruler. Hunger at Ra Cut and Sti Seam killed 35 people and displaced 189 over eleven years. The war with House Thream concluded without a treaty, leaving the border at Sti Seam contested. The Compact remained bound to the Kraeford Compact by marriage, but its military reputation was damaged by the loss of Kreagemoor and the failure to hold Sti Seam firmly against Thream’s repeated challenges.

The Kraeford Compact endured twenty years of shifting alliances and external pressure, beginning with a binding marriage to House Thream and ending with its ruler Wun Thu still in power despite a local uprising. The period opened with the Compact and House Thream swearing an alliance, followed by the marriage of Kraedren Waeld to Fous Bo, which formally tied the two powers together. This connection was severed when Kraedren Waeld had Skur Stas, the ruler of the Compact, murdered at Kraeford. Waeld’s subsequent challenge to the named heir Stearnke Gullleith failed in an election; Gullleith took the seat, and Waeld was cast out.

Gullleith’s rule was marked by violent retaliation against the Goummeidale Compact and internal instability. After the Goummeidale Compact raided Kraeford, the Kraeford Compact raided Goummeidale, carrying off 28 grain and killing 53. Gullleith survived a conspiracy by the exiled Waeld, who was declared outlaw. Gullleith died in 9, and Ma Graltaeld took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Frouldtoun Dror, who was cast out. Graltaeld’s tenure saw the Compact raid Kreagemoor and two unsuccessful raids on Sti Seam and Ra Cut. Graltaeld died in 12, and Wun Thu took the seat as no claimant remained.

Wun Thu’s rule was defined by a loss of standing and continued conflict with Goummeidale. In 12, Seithfaehollow rose against the Compact, whose standing had fallen very low. The Goummeidale Compact raided Kraeford and Seithfaehollow, carrying off plunder and killing many, while the Kreagemoor Covenant’s raid on Kraeford was beaten off. The Kraeford Compact sent out six raids in total: three carried off plunder, two got through but took nothing, and one was beaten off. It suffered five raids, four of which carried off plunder. One year of hunger at Seithfaehollow killed 69 people. The period ended with Wun Thu still holding the seat.

The Kreagemoor Covenant existed for thirty-one years, from its break with the Goummeidale Compact in year 8 to its destruction in year 37. It began as a breakaway settlement under Thral Rei and ended landless after its last ruler was killed and its followers scattered. The period was defined by internal instability, a devastating plague, and a final war against the Goummeidale Compact that the Covenant lost. Four people held the seat, passing it three times through election, death, and exile. The Covenant fought two battles, both lost to the Goummeidale Compact, and sent out five raids, all of which were beaten off.

Thral Rei took the seat in year 8 when Kreagemoor broke from the Goummeidale Compact. His rule ended in year 19 when he was murdered by Kraedren Waeld. Fous Bo contested the claim of the named heir Kraedren Waeld and took the seat by election. Fous Bo died in year 20. Frouldtoun Dror took the seat by election in year 20. Frouldtoun Dror had four people of other powers murdered at Goummeidale and Loufell between years 24 and 31. He was cast out in year 30 after an attempt on Skullhein Threill failed. Reafaeth Geall took the seat by election in year 30. Reafaeth Geall was killed by Skullhein Threill in year 37.

A plague broke out at Kreagemoor in year 14 and lasted four years, killing 320 people and driving 342 from their homes. The first year saw 56 dead. The second year saw 128 dead and 134 flee. The third year saw 89 dead and 135 flee. The fourth year saw 47 dead and 73 flee. The Covenant suffered five raids during this period, carrying off grain and killing residents. It also sent out five raids, all beaten off. Six exiles returned to take service with the Covenant.

The Goummeidale Compact declared war on the Covenant in year 36 over a long-standing grievance. The Goummeidale Compact and its allies defeated the Covenant at Kreagemoor in year 36, with 70 dead. They defeated the Covenant again at Kreagemoor in year 37, with 58 dead. The Goummeidale Compact took Kreagemoor from the Covenant in year 37. The Covenant was finished, its last 6 followers scattering. The Goummeidale Compact and the Covenant made peace in year 38.

The Goummeidale Compact’s twenty-year span from 22 to 41 was defined by violent internal succession and external expansion. Six people held the seat, each ruling for an average of 3.1 years, with the position passing five times. The period began with the Compact bound to House Thream through the marriages of Theirnpae Gro and Wold Risla in 22. Kaell Frouspim held the seat at the start, but his rule ended when he was killed by Frouldtoun Dror in 24. Wold Risla then took the seat, setting aside the claim of the named heir Freindmald Beindlea, who was cast out. Wold Risla was also killed by Frouldtoun Dror in 26.

Voumfaern Ki took the seat by right of birth in 26 but was killed by Frouldtoun Dror in 27. Maethhol Gondrur succeeded him but was murdered by Rateal Fototh in 28. Vasgou Raend took the seat, setting aside Rateal Fototh’s claim, but lost the seat to Skullhein Threill in 29 after an open challenge. Skullhein Threill held the seat until the end of the period. During this time, the Compact’s standing fell to nothing after Sti Seam rose against it in 28. The Compact sent three raids, all carrying off plunder, and fought four battles, all won. It took Kreagemoor from the Kreagemoor Covenant in 37 and Seithfaehollow from the Kraeford Compact in 40.

The Compact engaged in two wars, spending two years at war. It declared war on the Kreagemoor Covenant in 36 over a long-standing grievance, defeating them at Kreagemoor in 36 and 37. It declared war on the Kraeford Compact in 40, defeating them at Seithfaehollow in 40 and Kraeford in 41. The Compact ordered three killings against people of other powers: Reafaeth Geall in 37, Duthturn Tend in 39, and Soth Soulol in 41. One of its own people was murdered from within. Four people were cast out, and one exile returned. The Compact was bound to House Thream twice in 22 and to the Kraeford Compact twice, in 35 and 39.

Grigun Thrundeith took the seat of the Kraeford Compact in 50, following the exile of Saebull Kei. Kei had been cast out after an attempt on the life of Rateal Fototh failed and was traced back to him. The Goummeidale Compact had publicly slighted the Kraeford Compact earlier that same year. Thrundeith’s rise was possible because no claimant remained to contest the position.

In 51, Waeld Dould returned from exile and took service with the Kraeford Compact. The Goummeidale Compact declared war on the Kraeford Compact over a long-standing grievance. The Kraeford Compact spent 185 silver buying goodwill for the fourth time, but was not believed. The Goummeidale Compact defeated the Kraeford Compact at Kraeford, where 136 people died.

Theirnpae Gro took the seat of the Goummeidale Compact in year 51 by openly challenging and defeating Rateal Fototh. The victory was followed by the killing of Rateal at Goummeidale, an act recorded as a consequence of the challenge. Theirnpae’s rule was brief, ending in the same year.

The Goummeidale Compact declared war on the Kraeford Compact over a long-standing grievance. The conflict concluded with the Goummeidale Compact defeating the Kraeford Compact at Kraeford, where 136 people died. During this period, Thaeld Faeth was raised to heir of the Goummeidale Compact.

The War of the Goummeidale Compact's Grudge began in 36 when the Goummeidale Compact declared war on the Kreagemoor Covenant over a long-standing grievance. In that same year, the Goummeidale Compact and its allies defeated the Kreagemoor Covenant at Kreagemoor, where 70 people died. The conflict continued into 37, with the Goummeidale Compact and its allies defeating the Kreagemoor Covenant again at Kreagemoor, resulting in 58 deaths. Following this defeat, the Goummeidale Compact took Kreagemoor from the Kreagemoor Covenant.

During the fighting in 37, Skullhein Threill had Reafaeth Geall murdered at Kreagemoor. The war lasted for two years, ending in 38 when the Goummeidale Compact and the Kreagemoor Covenant made peace after the collapse of the Kreagemoor Covenant.

In year 3, the Goummeidale Compact declared war on House Thream for control of Sti Seam. The Compact defeated House Thream at Sti Seam that same year, with 35 dead. In year 4, House Thream defeated the Goummeidale Compact at Sti Seam, with 29 dead. In year 5, House Thream defeated the Goummeidale Compact at Sti Seam again, with 24 dead.

In year 6, the Goummeidale Compact defeated House Thream at Sti Seam, with 20 dead. The Compact took Sti Seam from House Thream. In year 7, the Goummeidale Compact and House Thream made peace after 4 years, both sides exhausted.
